title: Scaling equations for Bose-Einstein condensate dynamics across all interaction regimes
authors: D. C. Marinica, C. Puertas González, T. Estrampes, N. Gaaloul, E. Charron
abstract: We derive a unified set of scaling equations for Bose-Einstein condensates in time-dependent harmonic traps, connecting the weakly interacting Gaussian regime to the strongly interacting Thomas-Fermi regime. The exact Gross-Pitaevskii ground-state density is taken as a fixed profile in rescaled coordinates, with its dynamics described by three scaling factors corresponding to compression or expansion along the three spatial directions. The resulting equations contain no adjustable parameter, since their coefficients are determined once from the initial state. They recover analytically the Gaussian variational and Thomas-Fermi scaling equations in their respective limits and satisfy an axis-resolved virial theorem. The approach also yields the global phase and the low-lying collective-mode frequencies of the condensate. We benchmark the model against three-dimensional Gross-Pitaevskii simulations and against measured expansion energies. The model remains accurate across all interaction regimes, in strongly anisotropic traps, and along time-dependent sequences including a relatively fast quench, up to the point where the underlying frozen-profile hypothesis, shared by all three scaling approaches, breaks down.
summary: This paper develops a unified, parameter-free scaling theory for Bose-Einstein condensate dynamics in time-varying traps, bridging the gap between weakly and strongly interacting regimes. By assuming the condensate maintains its initial shape, the authors derive scaling equations that are validated against full numerical simulations. The model is highly valuable for predicting BEC behavior during complex, non-equilibrium experimental sequences.
main_problem: To derive a unified set of scaling equations that accurately describe the dynamics of Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs) across the entire spectrum of interaction strengths.
main_result: The authors present a parameter-free scaling model that analytically connects the weakly interacting Gaussian regime to the strongly interacting Thomas-Fermi regime, showing high accuracy across various trap dynamics.
method: The method uses a time-dependent variational principle and a scaling ansatz, assuming the condensate maintains the shape of its initial ground state profile.
model_or_system: The system is a BEC confined in a time-dependent harmonic trap, governed by the Gross-Pitaevskii Equation. The model derives equations of motion for three scaling factors ($\lambda_x, \lambda_y, \lambda_z$) based on global energy considerations.
key_observables: Scaling factors ($\lambda_j$), global phase, low-lying collective-mode frequencies, and expansion energies.
important_parameters: Interaction strength (connecting Gaussian and Thomas-Fermi limits), trap anisotropy, and the rate of trap change (quench speed).
main_assumptions: The core assumption is the 'frozen-profile hypothesis,' which posits that the condensate maintains its initial spatial shape, limiting the model's validity when higher-order modes are excited.
figures_summary: Figures compare the root-mean-square sizes ($\sigma_x, \sigma_{\perp}$) and the density profile $|\psi|$ derived from the scaling model against full 3D Gross-Pitaevskii simulations for both slow and fast trap ramps.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by deriving the scaling equations from the variational principle, demonstrating the recovery of known limits (Gaussian/TF), and concludes with extensive benchmarking against full numerical simulations to establish the model's domain of validity.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, analytically tractable, and parameter-free tool to model complex, non-equilibrium dynamics in BECs, which is crucial for understanding experimental quench dynamics in cold atom research.
